KZN FARMERS SECURING SAFETY

By: Nicky Troll | Production

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Farming Communities in KZN are taking their safety and security into their own hands with innovative and collaborative efforts to curb brutal farm attacks.

Unique Selling Point:
- FARM ATTACKS HOT TOPIC
- A DIFFERENT WAY TO DEAL WITH AN EMOTIVE TOPIC THAT OFFERS SOME LIGHT AT THE END OF THE TUNNEL
- COLLABORATION AND TECHNOLOGY MAKING A DIFFERENCE

Summary:
For years there’s been talks of the Rural National Safety Plan. It’s been reviewed and has supposedly been implemented. But farming communities in KZN are done waiting for a national plan to keep them safe. They have joined forces within the community and are fighting the violent scourge of farm attacks – using a community funded network of cameras, local security companies and farming associations expertise to track down the culprits and bring them to book.

They may not be able to completely prevent these attacks, but they are working around the clock to ensure that justice is served.


Further information:
While KZN farm attack stats are down , there’s been a rise in farm murders , with 15 recorded in the last year. But beyond the figures, is the nature of the attacks…they’re brutally violent.

By mid-April 2021 there has been nine attacks on farmers in KZN since the beginning of the year with three people murdered.

Considering the rural nature of the farm locations – the geography could be a contributing factor to the level of violence the farm attacks are carried out with. The attacker have the time to torture victims to open safes and if their intention is simply to exercise violence for whatever reason (mental disorders, vengeance, rape, etc.) there is less urgency than if this took place in an urban setting where the neighbours could be alerted.

In many cases there are large sums of case on the farm premises to pay suppliers and staff, making it a lucrative target. Often firearms that are stolen and re-used in other crimes.

ECONOMIC IMPACT
Every farm that stops being economically active after a farm attack or murder costs the SA economy an estimated R2 million – not taking into account the livelihood of farm workers and other businesses that supply services or products to those affected farms. This according to Guido Urlings - support services manager of community safety at Afriforum.

Thoko Didiza – National Minister of Agriculture, land reform and rural development said _ “ I would like to reiterate that an attack on a farmers is an attack on the country’s food security. Their role is very important ensuring a sustainable food production for the nation and the continent at large.

Provincial Agriculture and Rural Development MEC Bongi Sithole-Moloi’s office is committed to get to the bottom of their concerns and challenges and to find a way forward on how to resolve their problems.
Improved policing in the area will be “the number one priority” as “police were accused of taking sides in their investigations of crime within the farming community”.
“We cannot ignore the killing of farmers… We are interested in finding a lasting solution to this issue and to ensure that those who have committed these heinous crimes are arrested and convicted to long sentences,” KwaZulu-Natal Premier Sihle Zikalala said.
Zikalala said farm murders were an indication of unresolved and deep-seated issues around land ownership and land poverty as well as the country’s racist past.
“Either way, farmers, farm workers and farm dwellers are central to finding permanent solutions to every issue.
“Farm murders have become a real issue for our democracy and a concern, not only for the ruling party the ANC, but also an issue in our Legjslatures and Parliament, and among members of society in general, ” Zikalala said.
POLICE POSITION
Though Police Minister Bheki Cele refused to declare farm murders as a priority crime , he has claimed that the SAPS has ploughed in resources to deal with farm murders. He claimed that all incidences in rural areas, including farms and small holdings are analysed weekly, rural safety coordinators have been appointed to coordinate all activities within the rural policing area and to implement the National Rural Safety Plan.

According to Cele there are committees set up to monitor violence on farms and small holdings to establish trends and new developments and to plan preventative interventions and operations.

** COULD INTERVIEW KZN SAPS BUT I THINK WE’d BE BETTER OFF ASKING LOCAL GOVERNMENT FOR AN INTERVIEW – EITHER THE PREMIER OF THE MEC – KEEPING IT LOCAL AND REVELANT.

AGRISA POSITION
The Organisation believes that there are challenges in implementing the National Rural Safety Plan and in the current form it is just a rehash of old safety plans. They feel there is a general lack of support for farmers – both from a policing standpoint and a prosecutorial standpoint. From a government perspective the reality is that there are not enough resources to implement this plan. An National Rural Safety

WHAT’s HAPPENING IN KZN
KWANALU, KZN Agricultural Union, is a grassroots union linked to AgriSa that represents farmers across the spectrum. BOBBY HOOLE is on the board and works with the farming associations. They work closely with local communities, security companies and a non-profit organisation that has help fund CCTV vehicle license recognition cameras that cover 97% of the roads in the KZN Midlands region.

He believes it is crucial to realise that getting an arrest and successful prosecution does not mean justice is served, these criminals will be up for parole in a few years and it is vital that these cases are monitored and opposed to ensure that justice continues to be served.

SUCCESS OF COLLABORATION
The KZN Farming community has a network that connects 85 farming associations and security companies – within 3-7 minutes of an attack being reported on the group a response team can be activated. It is crucial for the team to secure the crime scene and ensure the chain of evidence collection is carried out properly.

Through their data collection, Brian Jones has developed a database that has compiled research and information from farm attacks in the region – collating information they are able to provide non-emotive, analytical data confirming crime trend, modus operandi’s and motives related to these attacks. For example, at least one of the assailants will be known to the victims, they will come on foot from a 4km radius, the majority of these cases are relationship driven and not race driven. Usually cars are taken from the farms as the getaway vehicles – and this is key to catching the criminals.

Using the network of cameras, the licence plate numbers are entered, tracked and traced. Just in April – the criminals were arrested within hours of an attack, while a second group of 8 that carried out a separate attack days later were also arrested in a couple of days through the collaborative efforts of the security industry, farming community and local police.

POLICE NOT COMPLETELY USELESS
On a local level the cops are hands on and part of the collaborative efforts. The issue is nationally the role of out a rural safety plan is over ambitious but on a smaller regional level this type of crime can be fought and results are possible.

EXTERNAL EXPERT OPTION - ISS
Johan Burger – Policing expert ISS. He has had some controversial ideas when it comes to dealing with farm attacks, and has really lambasted government for its snail-paced approach in dealing with this. He has suggested the introduction of Commandos in rural areas, the formation of an intelligence arm within the SAPS , to deal with farm attacks and the prioritisation of farm attacks across the country. Could be a good springboard interview into the need for smaller regional plans to be implemented.

CASE STUDY - THE RAFFERTY’s
On the 29th of August 2020, a thousand bikers marched to the Union Buildings in Pretoria to highlight farm murders in the country. On the same day a husband and wife were shot and killed during a farm attack in the Normandien area.

Glen and Vida Rafferty returned home to their farm at around 10.30pm on Saturday evening, where they were overpowered and killed by a group of attackers at the entrance to the property. It is believed the Rafferty’s dog was also shot. The attackers fled the farm in the couple’s vehicle which was abandoned on the N11 between Newcastle and Ladysmith.

Forensic teams were on scene taking fingerprints and collecting data from the vehicle in hopes that the attackers can be traced. A few weeks later, an arrest was made. The family has been left reeling from the attack losing both parents in a brutal attack. Would be a strong interview because there has been some success with arrests.

INTERVIEWS
- CASE STUDY – RAFFERTY FAMILY
- JOHAN BURGER – ISS – NATIOANAL PERSPECTIVE ON CURRENT STATE OF PLAN
- BOBBY HOOLE – LOCAL PERSPECTIVE // JUSTICE A LONG GAME
- BRIAN JONES – THE MAN ON THE GROUND - TRACK & TRACING, SUCCESS CASES, COLLABORATIVE SECURITY EFFORT
- KZN LOCAL GOVERNMENT – PMB

EXTRA aBUDGET
** FLIGHT FOR PRESENTER TO DBN
** ACCOMMODATION – Crew of 4 overnight in midlands, one night in Durban on Tuesday for Presenter – we won’t make it back for a flight – it’s a two- three hour drive to the midlands and we’ll be travelling a lot in between interviews.
** KILOMETERS TRAVELLED – we’ll use my car – more space for gear.

Press Release:




KZN Farmers Take Back Their Security

Agriculture Minister Thoko Didiza has called an attack on farmers an attack on the country’s food security. A Rural National Safety Plan has long been mooted, but where are the results? With 15 recorded murders on KwaZulu-Natal farms in the last year, farmers are coming together to take their safety into their own hands. Through a community-funded network of cameras, security companies and farming associations, the farmers are equipping themselves to track down farm murderers and bring them to book. But as the communities step up, Carte Blanche sits down with Premier Sihle Zikalala to ask where government fits into the equation.

Producer: Nicky Troll | Presenter: Macfarlane Moleli

Script:


STRUCTURE

VO: The 2020 South African Police Crime Stats recorded 21,325 murders across the country. That’s the unlawful premeditated killing of more than 21000 people.

LINK: Of those, 63 people were murdered in farm attacks. It may seem like insignificant number – but these attacks are often brutal and vicious – and the impact is far reaching.

VO: 15 of those farm murders were in Kwazulu Natal, the highest number for any province in 2020. These figures all exclude farm attacks.

Bobby Hoole is from Kwanalu, an agricultural union representing commercial and emerging farmers, and rural landusers in KZN.

BOBBY: any farm attack within the province or within South Africa is close to heart. in the last 12 to 18 months, we have seen a spike in farm attacks. // not necessarily resulting in murder and tragedy.

LINK: This is such a beautiful and idyllic setting, it is difficult to imagine the heinous crime taking place in KwaZulu Natal almost don’t make sense. An owner of a restaurant was hacked to the death – he took 30 blows to the face with panga.

VO: Edi Neumeister was killed in June 2020. What His neighbour and friend, Lillian Nadrowski, witnessed at the crime scene will haunt her forever.

LILLIAN: it was very clear that Eddie had put up one hell of a fight for his life.//the brutality with the loss of blood and the and the extent of the crime scene

VO: Edi’s fiance heard the struggle from their bedroom and looked out the window.

LILLIAN: // she saw the the panga come down on him and realized there was a there was an attack happening.

VO: When Edi’s Fiance tried to escape, the attacker turned his attention to her, leaving Edi to bleed out.

LILLIAN: // Eddie managed to to get himself up and and make his way into the house and one can only presume to to try and protect her. We could very clearly see the blood trail, follow his footsteps, bloody footsteps along along this pathway

VO: The attacker had gotten to Edi’s Fiance, strangling her with his hands as Edi eventually caught up.

LILLIAN: // it was at that point that he turned his attention back to Eddie, which gave her the opportunity to run out the back.W5M1



VO: Edi Neumeister fought till he couldn’t any more – and died on the scene.

From April 2020 to April 2021 there’s been between 30 and 40 farm attacks in KZN with 14 murders.

Trevor Murphy Friday, 23 April 21
Neil McKay Friday, 09 April 21
Graham Gibson Tuesday, 30 March 21
Danie & Glynis de Bruin Monday, 14 December 20
Colin Schwegman Monday, 14 December 20
Neville Theron Saturday, 12 December 20
Mpozana Khumalo Saturday, 14 November 20
Wendy Wilson Saturday, 07 November 20
Makatleo Sefoloko Vida & Glen Rafferty
Vida and Glen Rafferty
Hilton Dowdall
A pregnant Zakiyya Ismail
Koos Botha

Were all killed.

LINK: Every farm that stops operating after a farm attack or murder costs the South African economy - farm workers, suppliers and service providers loose a valuable income stream when the victims of these attacks call it a day and stop farming.

BOBBY: //A downscale in agricultural productivity here in South Africa that has an immediate knock on in terms of our food security for our country, but most of all, it has a socio economic impact

VO: KZN Premier Sihle Zikalala says this type of crime can not be tolerated.

PREMIER: // no one no one has a right to take someone else's life //M1 It is important that we deal with this because // you get farmers being killed// farming community then live in fear.

VO: The National Rural Safety Strategy has been on the cards for years, it’s meant be the solution to these brutal attacks in remote areas. Dr. Johan Burger is from the Institute for Security Studies.

BURGER: //broadly speaking, I think the national rural state, that strategy isn't really coming off the ground in the way that we were promised it would.

VO: Having reviewed the strategy, Dr. Burger notes although it’s a good practical strategy, it still falls short.

BURGER: The national commissioner has committed himself to working with organized agriculture in terms of setting up integrated operational centres nationally and provincially, locally, that will be manned by the police as well as by private security officials and organized agriculture. My information is none of these are in place. M14


VO: But farming communities in KZN are done waiting for a national plan to keep them safe.

Brian Jones from Toghether SA CAN, a community crime prevention organisation - has been analysing KZN cases over the past decade..

BRIAN: the only way in which you can create an overall plan is if you respond to the latest modus operandi, the latest trend with the latest technology

VO: And that’s what’s happening in KZN. The farmers have joined forces with the local security industry, regional police and provincial government - and they, are, making inroads.

BOBBY: we've started an initiative known as the Midland Security Task Team to ensure that all parties to to crime prevention and the ongoing investigations sit around the table. And we are all made aware of the issues at hand. Because what happens 100 kilometers away may soon be on our own doorstep.

VO: In many cases, there are safes on the farm property with cash, valuables and often firearms. The attackers will stop at nothing to get access to the loot.

LINK: One of the biggest contributing factors here is that farmers are isolated and response times to get to a scene takes long and here minutes could be the difference between a farm attack and murder LINK ISOLATION

VO: Urban areas are densely populated, criminals run the risk of neighbours, security or the police being alerted. Farming communities do not have this advantage.

BURGER: // So the criminals believe that they have all the time in the world to carry out the attacks. // they often torture victims. Usually this is to extract information

VO: With limited police resources, it’s up to community driven initiatives to fill those gaps.

Radio network communication is an essential part of the KZN safety and security strategy - connecting farmers in distress, with help.

First on the scene are often neighbouring farmers, who jump into action without hesitation, knowing that disrupting the attack, is crucial for survival. The average response time is under 10 minutes.

BRIAN: //, the truth of it is, is that if you just shone a torch, the suspects would run.

RYAN: Not all vehicles will descend on the scene. OK, several other vehicles// will actually go and park strategic points because unfortunately, nine out of 10 times the suspects have already left the scene.

VO: Ryan Carpenter is from a local security company dealing with these incidents.

RYAN: With all those eyes and ears on the ground and the information that's getting passed through very quickly, we’ve had some good successes



VO: Using a community funded network of vehicle license recognition cameras, that cover 97% of the roads in the KZN region, criminals are tracked and traced.

Jones has helped develop the Specialized Victim Support platform that collates all the evidence based data from KZN farm attacks and murders.

BRIAN: //There's also some very smart algorithms that power that network. So it's not just about the camera, it's about the analytics, we measure every single pulse point that happens. //It's either a verified piece of information or unverified

VO: Just in April – two groups of criminals that perpetrated farm attacks were arrested within hours of the one attack and a few days later in the second incident where Trevor Murphy was killed. The average arrest happens within 14 days to a month in KZN.

While They may not be able to completely prevent these attacks, they are working around the clock to ensure that justice is served, explains Hoole.

BOBBY: we are now able to fully understand from the minute the crime occurred right through to prosecution and understand terms of sentence and eventually get to to when the prisoners are offered parole// So it's a it's become not only a reporting matter now is the structures are following it all the way through to to the end.

VO: In every one of the KZN cases analysed by Jones, at least one of the attackers has a criminal record and at least one lived within four kilometers of the crime scene.

BRIAN: we've had relationship driven murders,// so it means that the victims and the perpetrators know one another prior to the events of the murder

VO: 80 year old livestock farmer, Mpozana Khumalo from the Nkomba area in KZN, was attacked on his land in November 2020 by two young men that he knew.

Speaking to his son Philamon, we learnt that the assault had stemmed from an argument about dogs.

PHILAMON: // They asked for water and then they grabbed him and forced him down by the tree. // They asked him about the dog. FLORIS PHUZA IS AFGENSY

VO: Khumalo’s hands were tied behind his back, he was beaten. Then shot in the arm and left for dead. He died a few days later in hospital, succumbing to his wounds.

The family is still struggling to come to terms with Khumalo’s murder.

PHILAMON: // if it were up to me, I would have taken action to avenge my father because the police aren’t doing anything. Now, I don’t know if it’s a good thing to kill each other

VO: The KZN Provincial Government are being proactive taking an arbitration role by implementing a programme called Community in Dialogue, to address relationship challenges in the farming sector.

PREMIER: Incidents of killing of farmers, serious exploitation of workers, undermine the progress.// It started as a blame game // but in some cases now you will see that there is a realization that they need each other.

VO: But The relentless onslaught of Violent crime seems endless for those affected unless justice is served.

LILLIAN: I think farmers // they are not being looked after. // unless there's real consequence to murdering someone, I can't see how it's going to stop.




PROMOS

PROMO 1
VO: Farming communities in KwaZUlu-Natal have taken their safety and security into their own hands - we investigate the effect of innovative and collaborative efforts to curb brutal farm attacks and bring the perpetrators to book.

PROMO 2:
VO: Farming communities in KZN are done waiting for a national plan to protect them against violent crime. Using innovative and collaborative networks, they are leading the way with their own safety and security strategy.

PROMO 3:
VO: Through a community-funded network of cameras, security companies and farming associations, KwaZulu-Natal farmers are equipping themselves to track and trace the assailants behind farm attacks [and murders to bring them to book.]

A Rural National Safety Plan has long been mooted, but where are the results? With 15 recorded murders on KwaZulu-Natal farms in the last year, farmers are coming together to take their safety into their own hands. Through a community-funded network of cameras, security companies and farming associations, the farmers are equipping themselves to track down farm murderers and bring them to book. But as the communities step up, Carte Blanche sits down with Premier Sihle Zikalala to ask where government fits into the equation. Producer: Nicky Troll | Presenter: Macfarlane Moleli Script: STRUCTURE VO: The 2020 South African Police Crime Stats recorded 21,325 murders across the country. That’s the unlawful premeditated killing of more than 21000 people. LINK: Of those, 63 people were murdered in farm attacks. It may seem like insignificant number – but these attacks are often brutal and vicious – and the impact is far reaching. VO: 15 of those farm murders were in Kwazulu Natal, the highest number for any province in 2020. These figures all exclude farm attacks. Bobby Hoole is from Kwanalu, an agricultural union representing commercial and emerging farmers, and rural landusers in KZN. BOBBY: any farm attack within the province or within South Africa is close to heart. in the last 12 to 18 months, we have seen a spike in farm attacks. // not necessarily resulting in murder and tragedy. LINK: This is such a beautiful and idyllic setting, it is difficult to imagine the heinous crime taking place in KwaZulu Natal almost don’t make sense. An owner of a restaurant was hacked to the death – he took 30 blows to the face with panga. VO: Edi Neumeister was killed in June 2020. What His neighbour and friend, Lillian Nadrowski, witnessed at the crime scene will haunt her forever. LILLIAN: it was very clear that Eddie had put up one hell of a fight for his life.//the brutality with the loss of blood and the and the extent of the crime scene VO: Edi’s fiance heard the struggle from their bedroom and looked out the window. LILLIAN: // she saw the the panga come down on him and realized there was a there was an attack happening. VO: When Edi’s Fiance tried to escape, the attacker turned his attention to her, leaving Edi to bleed out. LILLIAN: // Eddie managed to to get himself up and and make his way into the house and one can only presume to to try and protect her. We could very clearly see the blood trail, follow his footsteps, bloody footsteps along along this pathway VO: The attacker had gotten to Edi’s Fiance, strangling her with his hands as Edi eventually caught up. LILLIAN: // it was at that point that he turned his attention back to Eddie, which gave her the opportunity to run out the back.W5M1 VO: Edi Neumeister fought till he couldn’t any more – and died on the scene. From April 2020 to April 2021 there’s been between 30 and 40 farm attacks in KZN with 14 murders. Trevor Murphy Friday, 23 April 21 Neil McKay Friday, 09 April 21 Graham Gibson Tuesday, 30 March 21 Danie & Glynis de Bruin Monday, 14 December 20 Colin Schwegman Monday, 14 December 20 Neville Theron Saturday, 12 December 20 Mpozana Khumalo Saturday, 14 November 20 Wendy Wilson Saturday, 07 November 20 Makatleo Sefoloko Vida & Glen Rafferty Vida and Glen Rafferty Hilton Dowdall A pregnant Zakiyya Ismail Koos Botha Were all killed. LINK: Every farm that stops operating after a farm attack or murder costs the South African economy - farm workers, suppliers and service providers loose a valuable income stream when the victims of these attacks call it a day and stop farming. BOBBY: //A downscale in agricultural productivity here in South Africa that has an immediate knock on in terms of our food security for our country, but most of all, it has a socio economic impact VO: KZN Premier Sihle Zikalala says this type of crime can not be tolerated. PREMIER: // no one no one has a right to take someone else's life //M1 It is important that we deal with this because // you get farmers being killed// farming community then live in fear. VO: The National Rural Safety Strategy has been on the cards for years, it’s meant be the solution to these brutal attacks in remote areas. Dr. Johan Burger is from the Institute for Security Studies. BURGER: //broadly speaking, I think the national rural state, that strategy isn't really coming off the ground in the way that we were promised it would. VO: Having reviewed the strategy, Dr. Burger notes although it’s a good practical strategy, it still falls short. BURGER: The national commissioner has committed himself to working with organized agriculture in terms of setting up integrated operational centres nationally and provincially, locally, that will be manned by the police as well as by private security officials and organized agriculture. My information is none of these are in place. M14 VO: But farming communities in KZN are done waiting for a national plan to keep them safe. Brian Jones from Toghether SA CAN, a community crime prevention organisation - has been analysing KZN cases over the past decade.. BRIAN: the only way in which you can create an overall plan is if you respond to the latest modus operandi, the latest trend with the latest technology VO: And that’s what’s happening in KZN. The farmers have joined forces with the local security industry, regional police and provincial government - and they, are, making inroads. BOBBY: we've started an initiative known as the Midland Security Task Team to ensure that all parties to to crime prevention and the ongoing investigations sit around the table. And we are all made aware of the issues at hand. Because what happens 100 kilometers away may soon be on our own doorstep. VO: In many cases, there are safes on the farm property with cash, valuables and often firearms. The attackers will stop at nothing to get access to the loot. LINK: One of the biggest contributing factors here is that farmers are isolated and response times to get to a scene takes long and here minutes could be the difference between a farm attack and murder LINK ISOLATION VO: Urban areas are densely populated, criminals run the risk of neighbours, security or the police being alerted. Farming communities do not have this advantage. BURGER: // So the criminals believe that they have all the time in the world to carry out the attacks. // they often torture victims. Usually this is to extract information VO: With limited police resources, it’s up to community driven initiatives to fill those gaps. Radio network communication is an essential part of the KZN safety and security strategy - connecting farmers in distress, with help. First on the scene are often neighbouring farmers, who jump into action without hesitation, knowing that disrupting the attack, is crucial for survival. The average response time is under 10 minutes. BRIAN: //, the truth of it is, is that if you just shone a torch, the suspects would run. RYAN: Not all vehicles will descend on the scene. OK, several other vehicles// will actually go and park strategic points because unfortunately, nine out of 10 times the suspects have already left the scene. VO: Ryan Carpenter is from a local security company dealing with these incidents. RYAN: With all those eyes and ears on the ground and the information that's getting passed through very quickly, we’ve had some good successes VO: Using a community funded network of vehicle license recognition cameras, that cover 97% of the roads in the KZN region, criminals are tracked and traced. Jones has helped develop the Specialized Victim Support platform that collates all the evidence based data from KZN farm attacks and murders. BRIAN: //There's also some very smart algorithms that power that network. So it's not just about the camera, it's about the analytics, we measure every single pulse point that happens. //It's either a verified piece of information or unverified VO: Just in April – two groups of criminals that perpetrated farm attacks were arrested within hours of the one attack and a few days later in the second incident where Trevor Murphy was killed. The average arrest happens within 14 days to a month in KZN. While They may not be able to completely prevent these attacks, they are working around the clock to ensure that justice is served, explains Hoole. BOBBY: we are now able to fully understand from the minute the crime occurred right through to prosecution and understand terms of sentence and eventually get to to when the prisoners are offered parole// So it's a it's become not only a reporting matter now is the structures are following it all the way through to to the end. VO: In every one of the KZN cases analysed by Jones, at least one of the attackers has a criminal record and at least one lived within four kilometers of the crime scene. BRIAN: we've had relationship driven murders,// so it means that the victims and the perpetrators know one another prior to the events of the murder VO: 80 year old livestock farmer, Mpozana Khumalo from the Nkomba area in KZN, was attacked on his land in November 2020 by two young men that he knew. Speaking to his son Philamon, we learnt that the assault had stemmed from an argument about dogs. PHILAMON: // They asked for water and then they grabbed him and forced him down by the tree. // They asked him about the dog. FLORIS PHUZA IS AFGENSY VO: Khumalo’s hands were tied behind his back, he was beaten. Then shot in the arm and left for dead. He died a few days later in hospital, succumbing to his wounds. The family is still struggling to come to terms with Khumalo’s murder. PHILAMON: // if it were up to me, I would have taken action to avenge my father because the police aren’t doing anything. Now, I don’t know if it’s a good thing to kill each other VO: The KZN Provincial Government are being proactive taking an arbitration role by implementing a programme called Community in Dialogue, to address relationship challenges in the farming sector. PREMIER: Incidents of killing of farmers, serious exploitation of workers, undermine the progress.// It started as a blame game // but in some cases now you will see that there is a realization that they need each other. VO: But The relentless onslaught of Violent crime seems endless for those affected unless justice is served. LILLIAN: I think farmers // they are not being looked after. // unless there's real consequence to murdering someone, I can't see how it's going to stop. metadata.Summary: For years there’s been talks of the Rural National Safety Plan. It’s been reviewed and has supposedly been implemented. But farming communities in KZN are done waiting for a national plan to keep them safe. They have joined forces within the community and are fighting the violent scourge of farm attacks – using a community funded network of cameras, local security companies and farming associations expertise to track down the culprits and bring them to book. They may not be able to completely prevent these attacks, but they are working around the clock to ensure that justice is served.
metadata.Further information: While KZN farm attack stats are down , there’s been a rise in farm murders , with 15 recorded in the last year. But beyond the figures, is the nature of the attacks…they’re brutally violent. By mid-April 2021 there has been nine attacks on farmers in KZN since the beginning of the year with three people murdered. Considering the rural nature of the farm locations – the geography could be a contributing factor to the level of violence the farm attacks are carried out with. The attacker have the time to torture victims to open safes and if their intention is simply to exercise violence for whatever reason (mental disorders, vengeance, rape, etc.) there is less urgency than if this took place in an urban setting where the neighbours could be alerted. In many cases there are large sums of case on the farm premises to pay suppliers and staff, making it a lucrative target. Often firearms that are stolen and re-used in other crimes. ECONOMIC IMPACT Every farm that stops being economically active after a farm attack or murder costs the SA economy an estimated R2 million – not taking into account the livelihood of farm workers and other businesses that supply services or products to those affected farms. This according to Guido Urlings - support services manager of community safety at Afriforum. Thoko Didiza – National Minister of Agriculture, land reform and rural development said _ “ I would like to reiterate that an attack on a farmers is an attack on the country’s food security. Their role is very important ensuring a sustainable food production for the nation and the continent at large. Provincial Agriculture and Rural Development MEC Bongi Sithole-Moloi’s office is committed to get to the bottom of their concerns and challenges and to find a way forward on how to resolve their problems. Improved policing in the area will be “the number one priority” as “police were accused of taking sides in their investigations of crime within the farming community”. “We cannot ignore the killing of farmers… We are interested in finding a lasting solution to this issue and to ensure that those who have committed these heinous crimes are arrested and convicted to long sentences,” KwaZulu-Natal Premier Sihle Zikalala said. Zikalala said farm murders were an indication of unresolved and deep-seated issues around land ownership and land poverty as well as the country’s racist past. “Either way, farmers, farm workers and farm dwellers are central to finding permanent solutions to every issue. “Farm murders have become a real issue for our democracy and a concern, not only for the ruling party the ANC, but also an issue in our Legjslatures and Parliament, and among members of society in general, ” Zikalala said. POLICE POSITION Though Police Minister Bheki Cele refused to declare farm murders as a priority crime , he has claimed that the SAPS has ploughed in resources to deal with farm murders. He claimed that all incidences in rural areas, including farms and small holdings are analysed weekly, rural safety coordinators have been appointed to coordinate all activities within the rural policing area and to implement the National Rural Safety Plan. According to Cele there are committees set up to monitor violence on farms and small holdings to establish trends and new developments and to plan preventative interventions and operations. ** COULD INTERVIEW KZN SAPS BUT I THINK WE’d BE BETTER OFF ASKING LOCAL GOVERNMENT FOR AN INTERVIEW – EITHER THE PREMIER OF THE MEC – KEEPING IT LOCAL AND REVELANT. AGRISA POSITION The Organisation believes that there are challenges in implementing the National Rural Safety Plan and in the current form it is just a rehash of old safety plans. They feel there is a general lack of support for farmers – both from a policing standpoint and a prosecutorial standpoint. From a government perspective the reality is that there are not enough resources to implement this plan. An National Rural Safety WHAT’s HAPPENING IN KZN KWANALU, KZN Agricultural Union, is a grassroots union linked to AgriSa that represents farmers across the spectrum. BOBBY HOOLE is on the board and works with the farming associations. They work closely with local communities, security companies and a non-profit organisation that has help fund CCTV vehicle license recognition cameras that cover 97% of the roads in the KZN Midlands region. He believes it is crucial to realise that getting an arrest and successful prosecution does not mean justice is served, these criminals will be up for parole in a few years and it is vital that these cases are monitored and opposed to ensure that justice continues to be served. SUCCESS OF COLLABORATION The KZN Farming community has a network that connects 85 farming associations and security companies – within 3-7 minutes of an attack being reported on the group a response team can be activated. It is crucial for the team to secure the crime scene and ensure the chain of evidence collection is carried out properly. Through their data collection, Brian Jones has developed a database that has compiled research and information from farm attacks in the region – collating information they are able to provide non-emotive, analytical data confirming crime trend, modus operandi’s and motives related to these attacks. For example, at least one of the assailants will be known to the victims, they will come on foot from a 4km radius, the majority of these cases are relationship driven and not race driven. Usually cars are taken from the farms as the getaway vehicles – and this is key to catching the criminals. Using the network of cameras, the licence plate numbers are entered, tracked and traced. Just in April – the criminals were arrested within hours of an attack, while a second group of 8 that carried out a separate attack days later were also arrested in a couple of days through the collaborative efforts of the security industry, farming community and local police. POLICE NOT COMPLETELY USELESS On a local level the cops are hands on and part of the collaborative efforts. The issue is nationally the role of out a rural safety plan is over ambitious but on a smaller regional level this type of crime can be fought and results are possible. EXTERNAL EXPERT OPTION - ISS Johan Burger – Policing expert ISS. He has had some controversial ideas when it comes to dealing with farm attacks, and has really lambasted government for its snail-paced approach in dealing with this. He has suggested the introduction of Commandos in rural areas, the formation of an intelligence arm within the SAPS , to deal with farm attacks and the prioritisation of farm attacks across the country. Could be a good springboard interview into the need for smaller regional plans to be implemented. CASE STUDY - THE RAFFERTY’s On the 29th of August 2020, a thousand bikers marched to the Union Buildings in Pretoria to highlight farm murders in the country. On the same day a husband and wife were shot and killed during a farm attack in the Normandien area. Glen and Vida Rafferty returned home to their farm at around 10.30pm on Saturday evening, where they were overpowered and killed by a group of attackers at the entrance to the property. It is believed the Rafferty’s dog was also shot. The attackers fled the farm in the couple’s vehicle which was abandoned on the N11 between Newcastle and Ladysmith. Forensic teams were on scene taking fingerprints and collecting data from the vehicle in hopes that the attackers can be traced. A few weeks later, an arrest was made. The family has been left reeling from the attack losing both parents in a brutal attack. Would be a strong interview because there has been some success with arrests.
